title: Berkeley Math Tournament (BMT)
description: Student-run high school (and advanced middle school) mathematics competition hosted at UC Berkeley, featuring Power, Individual, and Guts rounds. Runs a separate middle-school event (BmMT) and a synchronous online format for students unable to travel to California.
verification_status: Verified - official page fetched and read (bmt.berkeley.edu 301-redirects to berkeley.mt; use berkeley.mt as the canonical URL)
research_notes: In-person BMT 2026 is Nov 14, 2026; a synchronous online format runs Dec 5, 2026 for students who can't travel; a separate middle-school BmMT Online runs June 6, 2026 (out of scope for high-school eligible_grades). No cost, deadline, selectivity mechanism, or explicit international-eligibility statement found on the official page -- left null rather than guessed. Org self-describes 'over 4,000 annual student participants from all across the globe' but that is marketing language, not a formal eligibility statement. selectivity_tier intentionally omitted (defaults to 'unknown') -- no acceptance-rate/nomination/exam gate found, but registration process itself was not explicitly confirmed either, so 'open_enrollment' would also be an unverified guess.

title: Stanford Math Tournament (SMT)
organization: Stanford Undergraduate Mathematics Organization (SUMO) / Stanford Department of Mathematics
description: Student-run high school mathematics tournament held on Stanford's campus (individual, team, power, and guts rounds), plus a separate SMT Online format open to middle and high school students worldwide.
current_cycle_label: 2026 (in-person event concluded Apr 17-18, 2026; 2027 dates not yet posted as of retrieval)
verification_status: Verified - official page fetched and read
research_notes: The official page's most current content describes the in-person SMT 2026 event (Apr 17-18, 2026), which has already concluded relative to this research's retrieval date (2026-08-21) -- no forward-pointing 2027 cycle statement was found, matching this research lane's own R4 finding that a past-dated page with no forward pointer is the most dangerous silently-stale case. SMT Online is described as 'open to all middle and high school students from anywhere in the world' -- a genuine international-eligibility statement, but scoped to the online format specifically, not confirmed for the in-person event. No cost, deadline, or selectivity mechanism found. start_date/end_date left null pending 2027 announcement rather than reusing the concluded 2026 dates.
